$comment: Rush Royale unit reference. Rendered by rushroyale.js on units.html. Authored order is Common -> Legendary and the page renders it as-is, so keep new entries in their rarity block. Fields: name, rarity (Common|Rare|Epic|Legendary), role (Damage|Support|Control|Summoner), damage (Physical|Magic|Poison|Mixed|None), summary (one plain sentence, no numbers), tags (search only), detail ('stub' draws the hatched marker). Every entry is a stub until someone checks it in-game and adds real figures — no numbers were invented here. This is not the full roster. Knight Statue, Kobold and Enchanted Swords were supplied by a player along with their role; their rarity is deliberately absent rather than guessed, so they show under All but under no rarity chip — add a 'rarity' key once it is confirmed.

entries.name: Archer
entries.summary: The unit you start with. Plain single-target damage at range, no special rule to learn — it is the baseline everything else is measured against.

entries.name: Bombardier
entries.summary: Lobs explosives that damage a small area rather than one enemy, so it earns its place on packed waves and wastes itself on single targets.

entries.name: Cold Mage
entries.summary: Chills what it hits, slowing enemies down. Its real value is buying time for your damage dealers, not the damage it does itself.

entries.name: Fire Mage
entries.summary: Area magic damage with a burn attached, so it keeps hurting after the hit lands.

entries.name: Hunter
entries.summary: A ranged attacker that catches more than one enemy at a time — a common early answer to waves that arrive in clumps.

entries.name: Lightning Mage
entries.summary: Its attack jumps between nearby enemies, so the more tightly packed the wave, the more total damage it does.

entries.name: Poisoner
entries.summary: Applies poison that ticks over time instead of hitting hard once. Good into things with a lot of health, poor into things that die instantly.

entries.name: Rogue
entries.summary: Single-target damage that leans on landing critical hits, so it gains a lot from anything that raises crit.

entries.name: Thrower
entries.summary: Straightforward thrown damage at a single target — cheap, reliable, and easy to merge because copies show up often.

entries.name: Alchemist
entries.summary: Every few seconds it drops a short-lived poison puddle on a random spot in the lane, damaging anything that walks through it. It does not aim, so it works best when the lane is busy.

entries.name: Banner
entries.summary: Deals no damage of its own. It buffs the units around it, which means where you place it matters more than what rank it is.

entries.name: Magic Cauldron
entries.summary: A support piece that works on a timer rather than by attacking — it does its job in the background while your damage dealers do theirs.

entries.name: Chemist
entries.summary: Built around poison. It is a payoff card: worth including when the rest of your deck already applies poison, close to wasted when it does not.

entries.name: Grindstone
entries.summary: Another placement-dependent support that sharpens the units near it instead of attacking. Put it in the middle of your damage, not in a corner.

entries.name: Priestess
entries.summary: A support unit that helps the board survive rather than clearing it. Most useful in co-op, where staying alive is the shared job.

entries.name: Sentry
entries.summary: Sits still and shoots what comes past. Predictable damage with no setup, which makes it a safe filler slot.

entries.name: Sharpshooter
entries.summary: Long-range single-target damage built around critical hits, so it pairs with anything that raises crit chance or crit damage.

entries.name: Zealot
entries.summary: A scaling unit — it gets stronger the longer it is on the board, so it rewards leaving it alone rather than merging it away.

entries.name: Crystalmancer
entries.summary: A ramping magic attacker: its attack speed climbs the longer it keeps firing at the same target, so it wants long waves and bosses.

entries.name: Engineer
entries.summary: Builds and maintains rather than attacking directly. A deck-shaping card — it changes what the rest of your board is doing.

entries.name: Executioner
entries.summary: Hits much harder against enemies that are already hurt, so it finishes waves other units have softened up.

entries.name: Wind Archer
entries.summary: Fast, light hits rather than heavy ones. It leans on attack speed, so buffs that add speed pay off more than buffs that add damage.

entries.name: Gargoyle
entries.summary: A sturdy attacker with a condition attached to its power — worth reading its card text carefully before building around it.

entries.name: Cold Elemental
entries.summary: Area damage plus an icy shard that makes a hit enemy take more damage each time it lands, and it hits harder still against enemies that are already stunned, slowed or paralysed.

entries.name: Earth Elemental
entries.summary: Periodically infects enemies so that any poison they take from any source hurts more. It is a multiplier for a poison deck, not a damage dealer on its own.

entries.name: Summoner
entries.summary: When you merge it, it summons a random unit from your deck onto a free tile at a rank somewhere between 1 and the Summoner's own merge rank — a way to fill the board without paying mana.

entries.name: Bard
entries.summary: A top-tier support that lifts the whole board rather than one lane. Widely treated as one of the strongest cards to invest in.

entries.name: Corsair
entries.summary: A high-end damage legendary that features in most current top decks.

entries.name: Genie
entries.summary: A flexible legendary that does useful work in a lot of different decks, which makes it a safe early legendary to level.

entries.name: Dryad
entries.summary: An all-purpose legendary commonly recommended as an early investment because it fits so many deck shapes.

entries.name: Wukong
entries.summary: A strong general-purpose damage legendary, regularly listed alongside Bard and Genie as a card worth levelling first.

entries.name: Valkyrie
entries.summary: A damage legendary built around a specific trigger condition rather than steady output.

entries.name: Monk
entries.summary: Uses reincarnation — it comes back after dying, which changes how you value the tile it occupies.

entries.name: Demon Hunter
entries.summary: Also uses reincarnation, pairing a damage role with the ability to return after dying.

entries.name: Lucia
entries.summary: A legendary damage dealer that shows up in current competitive lists.

entries.name: Knight Statue
entries.summary: Raises your carry's damage. One of the standard picks for the four support slots in a one-carry deck.

entries.name: Kobold
entries.summary: Also raises damage — the other name that comes up alongside Knight Statue when people describe the standard support shell.

entries.name: Enchanted Swords
entries.summary: Raises attack speed rather than damage, so the carry gets more hits in before the wave ends and the Phantom appears.

entries.name: Mountain Avens
entries.summary: Currently rated at the very top alongside Bard and Corsair.
